package_info.package_versions: All versions containing CVE-2021-44228 or CVE-2021-45046 vulnerabilities
package_info.why_malicious: Packages that directly include vulnerable Log4j code (either as shaded classes or as fat jars) are susceptible to remote code execution via Log4Shell, even if Log4j is not listed as a dependency. This hidden inclusion bypasses standard dependency scanning, leaving applications exposed.

execution_context.file_location: shaded Log4j classes within the package JAR

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code processes user-controlled log messages, evaluates JNDI lookups, and may resolve remote LDAP/HTTP resources, resulting in arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: JNDI lookups in log messages allow attackers to inject remote resource references, leading to code execution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal logging libraries should not resolve remote code or execute user-controlled input.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: JNDI lookups are used in enterprise Java for resource resolution, but not in log message evaluation.
key_indicators: Presence of JndiLookup class in shaded code
JNDI string parsing in log message processing

execution_context.file_location: log4j-core-*.jar included as a fat jar within the artifact

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: log4j-core-2.x.x.jar (vulnerable version) bundled inside the artifact
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the bundled vulnerable log4j-core jar enables JNDI-based log message evaluation, which can be exploited for remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Bundling a known-vulnerable jar exposes the application to well-documented exploits.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Artifacts should not include outdated or vulnerable third-party libraries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Fat jars are used for dependency packaging, but should be kept up-to-date and free of known vulnerabilities.
key_indicators: No corresponding dependency entry in build files

attack_chain.action: Vulnerable Log4j code is included directly in the artifact (either as shaded classes or as a bundled jar).
attack_chain.leads_to: Application is exposed to Log4Shell exploit vectors.

attack_chain.action: At runtime, attacker sends a crafted log message containing a JNDI lookup string.
attack_chain.leads_to: JNDI lookup is evaluated by the vulnerable Log4j code.

attack_chain.action: JNDI lookup triggers a remote resource fetch (e.g., LDAP/HTTP), potentially loading and executing attacker-controlled code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution on the victim system.

behavioral_signatures: JNDI string evaluation in log message processing
Network requests triggered by log message content
file_indicators: Shaded Log4j classes (org/apache/logging/log4j/core/lookup/JndiLookup.class) in application JARs
No corresponding dependency entry for Log4j in build files
network_indicators: Outbound LDAP/HTTP requests initiated during log message processing
Connections to attacker-controlled domains following log events
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan application artifacts for the presence of vulnerable Log4j classes or bundled jars, regardless of dependency declarations. Monitor for JNDI lookups in log message processing and unexpected outbound network requests triggered by log events. Use deep scanning tools that analyze both dependencies and embedded code.
